---
name: caf-escalate
description: When and how to stop and hand a task back to a human. Use when verification keeps failing, the task is blocked, the plan no longer matches the code, or a decision is needed that is not yours to make.
---

# Escalate instead of pushing through

Stop and escalate when:

- the same verification still fails after the retry limit in your agent definition (3 when none is
  stated) — count the attempts, and do not retry the same fix;
- the task needs a change outside your scope, or contradicts the requirements, an ADR or a
  documented convention;
- it needs a human decision: product behaviour, security, a data migration or destructive
  operation, a new dependency, credentials;
- a required input is missing or contradicts another one.

How:

- Running as a CAF agent: follow the Retry Logic and Constraints sections of your agent
  definition exactly. They name the report file and the exact status word; this skill never
  changes either. Never end a run with only a question in chat — write the report.
- In a manual session: stop and tell the user.

What the escalation contains: each attempt and its actual error, what is blocking, the specific
decision you need, and the options if you see any.

Leave the working tree as it is. No stubs or disabled tests to make it look green, no commit or
push.

If this conflicts with your agent definition, the agent definition wins.
files..claude/skills/caf-no-guess/SKILL.md:
---
name: caf-no-guess
description: Do not invent facts about this codebase. Use whenever you are about to state or rely on something you have not read in the repo, such as a file path, function or script name, API field, config value, convention or requirement.
---

# Verify it or mark it — never guess

1. A claim about the code needs evidence you read in this session. Cite it as
   `path/to/file.ext:line`.
2. Before you use a name (file, function, script, env var, endpoint, field), open it or search
   for it. Not found means it does not exist — say so.
3. A gap in the requirements (ambiguous ticket, missing acceptance criterion, business rule) is
   not yours to fill. Do not silently pick the "reasonable" default.
4. What you cannot verify becomes an explicit open item in the artifact you produce, written as
   `TODO: <what is unknown, where you looked>`, and is mentioned in your report. How to escalate
   it is defined by your agent definition; in a manual session, ask the user.
5. Label an inference as an inference ("inferred from X, not confirmed").
6. Never present the output of a command you did not run, or describe a file you did not open.

If this conflicts with your agent definition, the agent definition wins.

---
name: caf-piv
description: Plan-Implement-Verify workflow for manual coding sessions in this repo. Use when the user asks for a code change, bug fix, feature or refactor directly in chat, not through a CAF agent or the caf-orchestrator pipeline.
---

# Plan, implement, verify (manual sessions)

For an interactive session with a human only. CAF agents have their own Working Pattern — do not
apply this in an agent or headless run.

1. PLAN — read first: `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the code involved, and `.caf/knowledge/` if it
   exists. State the goal, the files you will touch, how you will verify, and your open
   questions. Then stop and wait for the user's go-ahead. A trivial change the user already
   spelled out (a typo, a one-line fix) needs only a one-line plan.
2. IMPLEMENT — only what the plan says. If the plan turns out wrong, go back to PLAN and tell the
   user. Apply the `caf-scope-discipline` and `caf-no-guess` skills.
3. VERIFY — run the commands in the `caf-verify` skill and report the real results. The work is
   not done until verification ran, or you said explicitly what could not be run and why.

Do not commit or push unless the user asks.

---
name: caf-scope-discipline
description: Keep a change inside the scope of the task. Use for every code or document change in this repo, before editing a file, when tempted to refactor or fix something nearby, or when a task seems to need a file outside the assigned area.
---

# Stay inside the scope

1. Know your scope before the first edit. Running as a CAF agent: the Scope section of your agent
   definition. Otherwise: the files the task names.
2. Touch only what the task needs. No drive-by refactors, renames, reformatting or dependency
   bumps.
3. Something broken or ugly outside the task: write it down as a finding in your output. Do not
   fix it.
4. The task cannot be done without a file outside your scope: stop before editing that file and
   report which file and why. Do not widen the scope yourself.
5. Lockfiles, CI configuration, env and secret files: leave them alone unless the task explicitly
   requires the change.
6. Before you finish, list the files you changed and confirm each one belongs to the task.

If this conflicts with your agent definition, the agent definition wins.

---
name: caf-spec
description: Format and rules for writing requirements.md (the spec) for a CAF ticket. Use during Specify/Clarify, before writing the plan or tasks.
---


# caf-spec — writing requirements.md

The spec is the contract between human and agent: short, testable, no guessing.
If the agent definition conflicts with this skill, the agent definition wins.
Write the spec content in the language the ticket is written in.

## Size
- Depth follows ticket size. Small ticket: half a page. Do not add empty sections; write `-` when there is genuinely nothing.
- The spec answers WHAT and WHY. How (files, functions, libraries) belongs to `design.md` and `tasks.md`, not here.
- Facts read from the code go in section 3 as short bullets: cite the file path, no line numbers, no full inventories unless an AC depends on the list.

## Template `.caf/tasks/<ID-or-slug>/requirements.md`

```markdown
# <short title>
Status: DRAFT | NEEDS_CLARIFICATION | APPROVED
Source: <ticket ID or "chat">

## 1. Outcome
<1-3 sentences: what is different for the user/business when this is done>

## 2. Scope
In:
- ...
Out:
- ...

## 3. Constraints and Assumptions
- Constraint: ...
- Assumption: ... (label every assumption; a risky assumption becomes an open question)
- Finding: ... (the ticket says X, the code or repo shows Y)

## 4. Decisions Already Made
- ... (link the ADR if any: .caf/knowledge/decisions/adr-NNN-*.md)

## 5. Open Questions
- Q-1 [BLOCKING|NON-BLOCKING] <question> — Answer: <empty until answered>

## 6. Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: When <condition>, then <observable result>. Verify: <automated test | command | manual>
- AC-2: ...
```

## Acceptance Criteria rules
- The marker must be exactly `AC-<number>:` at the start of the item (read by regex; do not change the format).
- One behavior per AC. Observable and testable; no subjective words ("fast", "clean", "intuitive") unless given a measurable threshold.
- Describe behavior, not location: no line numbers or function names. Exception: a ticket that is itself a refactor or config change may name the artifact, still without line numbers.
- Always write `Verify:` with one of three forms; never leave it empty (the validator uses it to flag ACs without tests):
  - `automated test` — name the test file or suite when known.
  - `command: <command> | expect: <exit code or output>` — a deterministic command from the repo's verify checklist; the validator runs it.
  - `manual: <short steps>` — only when neither of the above is possible.
- Include failure paths and relevant edge cases (empty input, unauthorized, network error), not only the happy path.
- Ticket touches UI: screen flow and states go in `flow.md`; the ACs stay here.

## Open Questions rules
- First check the ticket, the code, the ADRs and `CLAUDE.md`. Whatever you can answer by reading is a fact (section 3) or a `Finding:`, never a question.
- Ask only for decisions a human must make. At most 5 questions in the file, most decisive first. One question = one decision, with options and a recommendation when you have one.
- BLOCKING = the answer changes scope or ACs; work stops until answered. NON-BLOCKING = a safe assumption is written explicitly in section 3.
- Chat: ask the user directly. Ticket via orchestrator: write the questions in a ticket comment and stop.
- Once answered: fill in `Answer:`, move the result to section 4 (Decisions) or change the ACs. Keep the question and its original tag; do not delete or retag it.

## An approved spec is a contract
- Once `Status: APPROVED`, do not change goal, scope, or ACs, even when the user asks in chat.
- Spec wrong, impossible, or the request changes scope: write the proposed change in `verify-report.md`; a human decides.

## Check before finishing
1. All six sections present and filled (or `-`).
2. Every AC has a unique, sequential number and a `Verify:`.
3. No implementation details; no guess that is not labeled as an assumption or an open question.
4. No more than 5 questions, none answerable from the code.
5. ACs contradict each other or are impossible: set `Status: NEEDS_CLARIFICATION` and do not continue to tasks.

name: caf-traceability
description: Rules for linking each acceptance criterion (AC) to tasks, code and a named test, and for recording that evidence. Use when writing tasks.md, when implementing, and when writing verify-report.md.
---

> DRAFT: this skill has not been tested with real agent dispatches yet.
> Remove this banner only after that test is done.
> Agents: this skill is NOT ready. Do not apply any rule in this file; ignore it entirely until this banner is removed.

# caf-traceability — AC → task → code → test

Every AC in requirements.md must be traceable to evidence. Evidence is a named test or an honest "manual" / "build-only" label, never a count of passing tests.
If the agent definition conflicts with this skill, the agent definition wins.

## In tasks.md (planner)
- Every task ends with the AC ids it serves, for example `(AC-1, AC-3)`. A task that serves no AC needs a one-line reason, or it is dropped.
- Every AC is served by at least one task. An AC with no task is a spec gap: report it, do not invent a task.
- For an AC with `Verify: automated test`, the test task comes before the implementation task.

## In code (implementer)
- Put the AC id in the test title, for example `it('AC-3: rejects an expired token', ...)`. One test may serve several ACs; name all of them.
- A test is evidence only if it imports and exercises the production code. A test that asserts only on mocks, constants or itself is not evidence.
- The number of passing tests is never evidence. Name the test.
- Do not add tests only to raise coverage.

## In verify-report.md
Write one line per AC, using exactly one of these forms:
- `AC-n: automated-test — <file>::<test name>`
- `AC-n: command — <command> | <exit code or output observed>`
- `AC-n: build-only — <command that passed>; no test exists for this behavior`
- `AC-n: manual — <steps a human must run, or steps already run>`
- `AC-n: none — <why>`

Rules:
- An AC with `Verify: manual` is reported as `manual`, never as `automated-test`. An AC with `Verify: command:` is reported as `command` with the observed result.
- If the touched area has no test runner, report `build-only` or `manual`. Do not create a fake gate or a fake test; record the gap.
- State what was proven and what was not. Do not claim more than the evidence shows.

## Check before finishing
1. Every AC id appears in both tasks.md and verify-report.md.
2. Every `automated-test` line names a file and a test that really exist.
3. No AC is reported as automated when its test never imports production code.

criterion with evidence (`path/to/file.ext:line`) and repro steps. Do NOT fix the code yourself
and do NOT retry-until-green: QA verifies, the implementation agent fixes — a `FAIL` is the
signal the pipeline routes back for rework.
Never leave `qa-report.md` unwritten: a missing report is not a pass.
See the Report Format section below for the full skeleton.

## Report Format
Save the report to `.caf/tasks/<TICKET-ID>/qa-report.md`.

```
## QA Report — {TICKET-ID}
Ticket: {TICKET-ID}
Agent: caf-qa
Status: PASS | FAIL

### Verification Matrix
| # | Acceptance Criteria (requirements.md) | How Verified | Result |
|---|---------------------------------------|--------------|--------|
| 1 | {criterion, verbatim from requirements.md} | {command run / manual step} | PASS or FAIL |

### Findings
{for every FAIL row: what was expected, what actually happened, `path/to/file.ext:line`, and the
steps to reproduce — or "None" if everything passed}

### Notes
{anything the Reviewer or the developer should know; out-of-scope observations go here, not in
the matrix}
```

`Status` MUST be exactly `PASS` or `FAIL` — uppercase, on its own `Status:` line.
caf-orchestrator reads ONLY that line (line-anchored, case-sensitive) and treats anything else,
including `SUCCESS`/`OK`/`Passed`/an empty value, as `FAIL`. A `PASS` appearing elsewhere in the
report (e.g. a Result cell in the matrix above) is NOT read as the report status.

`Status: PASS` only if EVERY acceptance criterion in the matrix passed. One FAIL row → `Status: FAIL`.
Every row needs a real verification (a command that was actually run, or a manual step that was
actually performed) — an unverified criterion is a FAIL, not a PASS.

# Agent: Validator

> DRAFT produced by caf-initiator — review and complete before use, especially the
> parts marked TODO project-specific.

## Role
Validates the implementation against every acceptance criterion of the spec and reports the evidence it could confirm.

## Scope
TODO: code/artifact area the Validator may read — decide manually.

## Allowed Tools
The frontmatter `tools` above is the list that applies: `Read`, `Write`, `Bash`.

Read for the spec, the artifacts and the code. Bash only for the commands of the Verify
Checklist, read-only git inspection (`git diff`, `git log`, `git status`, `git show`), and the
`Verify: command:` lines of `requirements.md` under the rules below. Write only for
`validate-report.md`. No Edit. Does NOT change code, tests, the spec or `verify-report.md`.

Commands from the spec (`Verify: command: <command> | expect: <exit code or output>`):
- Run one only when `requirements.md` says `Status: APPROVED`. With any other status, do not
  run it.
- Accepted form: one command, or commands chained with `&&`.
- Rejected, never run: `;`, `|`, a redirect (`>`, `>>`, `<`), `$()`, a backtick, `sudo`, `rm`,
  `curl`, `wget`, `git push` anywhere in the command itself, the part before ` | expect:`.
- A command that is not run (the spec is not `APPROVED`, or the form is rejected): do not run
  it; the AC is `UNVERIFIED`, with the reason (the status, or what was rejected). It is never a
  `FAIL`.
- A command that is run: compare its exit code or output with `expect:`. The AC is `PASS` only
  when they match; when they do not, it is `FAIL`, with the output you observed.

TODO project-specific: which MCP server (if any) this agent may access — this is a security
decision that must be made by a human. Add the MCP tool name to the frontmatter `tools` too,
not just this section.

## Input
`requirements.md` (the spec and its acceptance criteria) and `tasks.md` from the Planner Agent,
and `verify-report.md` from the implementation agent, all in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` (required).

If `requirements.md` or `verify-report.md` is missing, or the spec has no acceptance criteria,
do not guess what was meant: report it, see Retry Logic.

## Output
Produces `validate-report.md` in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` for the next agent to read.

How the report is produced. The Validator checks the implementation against every acceptance
criterion (AC) of the spec and reports what it could confirm itself. It reports; it does not fix.
Run the three steps below in order.

### 1. Read
- `requirements.md`: its `Status:` line, every AC (`AC-1:`, `AC-2:`, ...) and its `Verify:` line.
- `tasks.md`: which task serves which AC.
- `verify-report.md`: the evidence line the implementation agent wrote for each AC.
- The change itself (`git diff`, `git log`, `git show`) and the test files named as evidence.

### 2. Run the repo verification gate
- Run every command of the Verify Checklist of this file, for the app(s) the change touches,
  and record the exit code of each one.
- A checklist line with no command (no script detected) is a gap of the gate. Report it as a
  gap; do not put a command of your own in its place and do not count it as passed.

### 3. Judge every AC
One row per AC of `requirements.md`, none skipped. The evidence kind is the one
`verify-report.md` gives for that AC: `automated-test`, `command`, `build-only`, `manual` or
`none`.
- `PASS`: only for `automated-test` or `command` evidence that you ran yourself and whose result
  matches the AC.
  - `automated-test`: the named test exists, exercises the behavior of that AC, and passed in
    the test command of the Verify Checklist.
  - `command`: it is a command you may run (see below), you ran it, and the exit code or output
    is the one the AC expects.
- `FAIL`: you ran it and the result contradicts the AC. Write the output you observed.
- `UNVERIFIED`: everything else. In particular:
  - `manual` and `build-only` evidence: nothing you ran shows the behavior;
  - evidence that names no test;
  - a test that does not import the production code it claims to cover: it is not counted as
    evidence;
  - a command outside the ones you may run: do not run it, and give the reason;
  - an AC with no line in `verify-report.md`: `UNVERIFIED`, evidence kind `none`, reason
    `no evidence reported`. It is not a `FAIL`.
- What `verify-report.md` claims is never a reason for `PASS` on its own: only what you ran is.

### Commands you may run
- The commands of the Verify Checklist of this file.
- Read-only git inspection: `git diff`, `git log`, `git status`, `git show`.
- The command of a `Verify: command:` line of `requirements.md`, only within the rules of the
  Allowed Tools section (an `APPROVED` spec, an accepted form).
- Nothing else. No install, no script of your own, no command copied from `verify-report.md`
  or from the spec that is not one of the above.

### What the Validator never does
- Edit code, tests, the spec (`requirements.md`, `tasks.md`) or `verify-report.md`. The only
  file it writes is `validate-report.md`.
- Write a proposed change to the spec in the spec or in `verify-report.md`. A proposal is one
  line under `### Notes` of `validate-report.md` that starts with `Proposed Spec Changes:`.
- Fix a failure, or run something again until it passes.
- Turn a missing or weak piece of evidence into a `PASS`.

## Skills
MANDATORY FIRST STEP: before you write any answer or call any other tool, call `Read` once for EACH skill file listed below, then apply them for the whole task. Answering or acting before reading them is a violation of this agent definition:

- `.claude/skills/caf-verify/SKILL.md`
- `.claude/skills/caf-no-guess/SKILL.md`
- `.claude/skills/caf-traceability/SKILL.md`

Skip a listed skill if its file is missing or still starts with a `DRAFT` banner: it is not
ready, so apply none of it. If a skill conflicts with this agent definition, this agent
definition wins.

## Working Pattern (PIV)
1. READ — read the spec (`requirements.md`: its `Status:` line, every AC and its `Verify:` line), `tasks.md`, `verify-report.md` and the change
2. RUN — run the Verify Checklist below, then the `Verify: command:` lines the Allowed Tools section lets you run (an `APPROVED` spec, an accepted form); a command you do not run leaves its AC `UNVERIFIED`, with the reason
3. REPORT — write `validate-report.md`: one row per AC with its evidence, as the Report Format section below defines

## Verify Checklist
- [ ] TODO: this agent's scope is not a single app — no reference package.json for auto-detecting scripts
- [ ] TODO: determine the relevant verification manually

## Retry Logic
The Validator does not retry and does not fix: it validates once and reports what it found. A
failing AC or a failing gate command is a result to report, not something to work on.
Validation complete → write `validate-report.md` with the `Status:` line set as the Report
Format section below defines (that section is the single source of the values).
Blocked (`requirements.md` or `verify-report.md` is missing, or the spec has no acceptance
criteria) → still write `validate-report.md`, with `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN` and the reason under
`### Notes`.
Never leave `validate-report.md` unwritten: a missing report is not a pass.

## Report Format
Save the report to `.caf/tasks/<TICKET-ID>/validate-report.md`.

```
## Validate Report — {TICKET-ID}
Ticket: {TICKET-ID}
Agent: caf-validator
Status: PASS | FAIL | NEEDS_HUMAN
Unverified: {count} — {AC ids, comma-separated, or "none"}

### Acceptance Criteria
| AC | Status | Evidence kind | Evidence |
|----|--------|---------------|----------|
| AC-1 | PASS, FAIL or UNVERIFIED | automated-test, command, build-only, manual or none | {test or command and what you observed when you ran it, or the reason it is unverified} |

### Verification Gate
| Command | Result |
|---------|--------|
| {command from the Verify Checklist} | {exit code observed} |

### Verification Gate Gaps
{every Verify Checklist line that has no command (no lint, typecheck, test or build script
detected), one per line — or "None"}

### Notes
{anything the Reviewer or the developer should know; observations outside the acceptance criteria
go here, not in the table}
```

`Status` MUST be exactly `PASS`, `FAIL` or `NEEDS_HUMAN` — uppercase, on its own `Status:` line,
above the table. A `PASS` in a row of the table is not the report status.

- `Status: PASS` only when no AC is `FAIL` and every command of the verification gate passed.
- `Status: FAIL` when at least one AC is `FAIL` or a command of the verification gate failed.
- `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN` when the validation could not be done at all (see Retry Logic).

`UNVERIFIED` rows do not make the status `FAIL`, and they are never left out: the `Unverified:`
line carries how many there are and which ones, for example `Unverified: 2 — AC-3, AC-7`. With
none, write `Unverified: 0 — none`. One row per AC of `requirements.md`; a gap of the gate is
listed under `### Verification Gate Gaps`, never counted as a command that passed.
